name: Taba–Sharm El-Sheikh Gas Pipeline

values.OtherEnglishNames: South Sinai Gas Pipeline; Taba/Sharm El-Sheikh Line
values.RouteNotes: Runs south down the South Sinai east coast along the coastal road, Taba–Nuweiba–Dahab–Sharm El-Sheikh, serving en-route towns, hotels/tourist villages and the Taba, Nuweiba, Dahab and Sharm El-Sheikh power stations. No official GIS route located; corridor approximate.

researcher_notes:
MATCH-TO-EXISTING RE-CHECKED, NO MATCH: no GEM gas row runs south down the Sinai east coast. The two Sinai lines at the Taba node run opposite directions — P0436 (Arab Gas Pipeline, Arish→Taba) and P7482 (AGP Taba→Aqaba subsea). Hurghada–Safaga (P6034) is on the mainland Red Sea coast, not Sinai. So this coastal trunk is a genuine gap. NEW_ROW.

ADD-THRESHOLD MET (all three): (a) sponsor = GASCO/Egyptian Natural Gas Co; (b) country + endpoints = Egypt, Taba→Sharm El-Sheikh via Nuweiba & Dahab, South Sinai; (c) concrete step = built and operating since early 2007.

EXISTENCE — well corroborated (2+ independent): (1) OGJ (Sep 2007 trade journal) describes GASCO building the Taba/Sharm El-Sheikh line from 2006, 220 km of 20-inch pipe, up to 6 MMcfd, online early 2007 at ~L.E. 511M, serving en-route towns/hotels and the Taba, Nuweiba, Dahab and Sharm El-Sheikh power stations. (2) EDEPCO (Egyptian Distribution & Electricity, govt) page confirms the Sharm El-Sheikh power plant (~288 MW) is natural-gas-fired. (3) Youm7 (2021) confirms operating natural-gas distribution and CNG car stations across South Sinai (Sharm El-Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba, Taba). A gas-fired power station plus household/CNG gas across these coastal cities cannot be supplied without a transmission trunk down the coast from Taba — and no other GEM row provides one — independently corroborating that this corridor exists and operates.

SPECS — single-source (medium/low): the 220 km / 20-inch / ~511M EGP / 2007 figures rest solely on OGJ (tracing to GASCO); no independent second source on the numbers was found in EN or AR. Overall row tier = medium (existence high, attributes single-source).

CAPACITY DELIBERATELY OMITTED: OGJ's 'up to 6 MMcfd' is implausibly low — the Sharm gas power plant alone (~288 MW) needs far more than 6 MMcfd — likely a units/typo error in the single source. Left Capacity blank rather than stage a suspect value; flagged here for reviewer.

SOURCE REJECTED: the EIB/PETROSAFE 'GASCO Abr Sinai Onshore Gas Pipeline' EIA (eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_eia4_en.pdf) is a DIFFERENT pipeline — a 36-inch North Sinai loop, El-Tena East→El-Arish — not this South Sinai coastal 20-inch line; not cited.

OWNER: reused existing GEM entity 'Egyptian Natural Gas Co' (GASCO); entity_lookup matched it (score 93), no new entity created. Parent (EGAS/Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co) left blank — not independently verified for this specific line.

ROUTE: no official GIS located; corridor follows the South Sinai east-coast road Taba–Nuweiba–Dahab–Sharm El-Sheikh; RouteAccuracy = approximate. Route/geometry is a candidate for a separate human routes-repo PR, not staged here.
